title: Ajahn Funn: The four elements – earth, water, fire, wind – come together. The earth element: hair, body hair, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, tendons, bones,…
content:
The Four Elements: Earth, Water, Wind, Fire – Coming Together as a Person

The four elements – earth, water, fire, wind – come together. The earth element: hair, body hair, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, tendons, bones, liver, kidneys, small intestine, large intestine, old food, new food – whatever is hard in our body is called the earth element. The water element: bile, phlegm, sweat, lymph, mucus, saliva – whatever is liquid in our body is called the water element. The wind element: in-breath, out-breath, wind moving upward, wind moving downward, wind moving throughout the body – that is classed as the wind element. The fire element: that which warms our body, digests food, or ages and deteriorates the body – that is called the fire element.

When these four come together, it's called a person, a self. When there is a self, everyone has the four elements, the five aggregates, and the six sense spheres together. So why are people not the same? Some are low, some are dark or fair, some are big, some are small – not the same, not equal. Why? For this reason: they differ in virtue and qualities. This is it: we lack action.

title: Ajahn Funn: Why come see? Because we hold this to be self, to be a being, a person, a "me" or "him." Let us see…
content:
The Body Bounded by Skin, Filled with Impurities – Hair, Nails, Teeth, Skin

Why come see? Because we hold this to be self, to be a being, a person, a "me" or "him." Let us see whether it really is a self or a being, whether it really is a person. Where is the person? Is this "me" the person? Or are the hairs the person? Or the nails? Or the teeth? Or the skin? No, aren't they? Or is it the flesh? Or the bones? Or the liver, kidneys, small intestine, large intestine? Those are just names. Where is the person? We must know and see this. This is the point: let us all know kammaṭṭhāna. This is to see rūpa-dhamma and nāma-dhamma. The concocter, the fabricator — that is thinking, intending, mental objects, perceptions — that is nāma-dhamma, merely thinking and intending. Bring this to contemplation. Know "na" and know "mo". Only then can we protect our heart. If we do not know "na" and "mo", we cannot protect our heart.

The teaching says: Now, where are we a person? Tacapariyanto — bounded by skin all around. Pūrāṇānappakārassa asucino — filled with all kinds of impurities. Atthi imasmiṃ kāye — in this body. They do not say that other body; "this body" means pointing to each one of our own bodies. Filled with impurities.

title: Ajahn Funn: That is why we are taught to go to the temple. Nowadays, people don’t examine themselves at all. They are completely in the…
content:
Peace Is Happiness: There Is No Happiness Equal to Peace

That is why we are taught to go to the temple. Nowadays, people don’t examine themselves at all. They are completely in the dark. Therefore, they kill, slash, and stab each other without thinking of their own selves. Their own selves fear death; others also fear death. So don’t do it. If everyone knew this and practiced this, everyone would be at ease, the town would be peaceful, the country would be peaceful, the human world would be peaceful. Peace is happiness. There is no happiness equal to peace.

Therefore, from now on, perform this regular practice: go to the temple every day. Go to the temple and listen to Dhamma every day. Buddho, Dhammo, Saṅgho – our refuges are only these. Nothing else can be relied upon at all. If you know this, remember it. Go to the temple every day. Contemplate yourself so that you see within. See what is good, what is bad, what is happiness, what is suffering. When you see, doubt ends, and you have only confidence in the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Sangha. Then you have a refuge, a shelter. There is nothing in the world like it.

title: Ajahn Funn: Knowing this, quickly correct it right now. Don't let it pass even a moment. If you leave what is bad in place, then…
content:
The Root of All Good and Bad Is the Heart – Like the Root of a Tree

Knowing this, quickly correct it right now. Don't let it pass even a moment. If you leave what is bad in place, then you will remain a bad person. This is it. People blame this and that as bad, doing this is bad, doing that is bad. Why is it bad? We don't look at its origin. We don't look at its root. Where does the root come from? If the root is not good, how can the tip be good? We must look at its root – that is, this heart. This is the root. If the root is good, the fruit will be good. It's like a tree: if you take good care of the root, fertilize and water it well, the tree will be good, producing abundant flowers and fruit. The same here. If our heart is good, then everything we do becomes good. Whatever livelihood we pursue becomes good: trade, government service, family, relatives, neighbors, the country – all good. Whether ordained or not, if the heart is good, there will be no quarrels, no distress, only peace.

title: Ajahn Funn: That's how it is. If we don't unify, it doesn't get accomplished. There will still be "this is a defilement, that is craving,…
content:
Kamma Arises from Body, Speech, and the Heart – Not from the Sky or Mountains

That's how it is. If we don't unify, it doesn't get accomplished. There will still be "this is a defilement, that is craving, lust" – it's not finished. Unify it into a single mass. Only then can it be accomplished. This person does not send the mind forward or backward – so who would send it? "My mind isn't still; where does it go?" It doesn't actually go. The light goes. So don't say it goes; if you say it goes, it will go. Don't speak of it. Be calm, be still. Don't send it forward or backward. Just focus and look.

This is attainment: unifying our mind so that it becomes unified. If it unifies, attainment happens right there. If it doesn't unify, there is no attainment. All of you, focus and look. Opanayiko – bring it inward. Paccattaṁ – known only by each one for themselves. This is what people call kamma. Where is kamma?

The Buddha did not teach that kamma lies in the sky, air, mountains, or forests. He said in the Jayamaṅgala Gāthā: kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ manokammaṃ – kamma arises from body, from speech, and from the heart. Kamma is here. It doesn't come from anywhere else.

title: Ajahn Funn: I'll give you a simple analogy, like building a hall. Have you finished building the hall? When it's finished, what is it? When…
content:
The Simile of Building a Hall: Unifying the Mind into One

I'll give you a simple analogy, like building a hall. Have you finished building the hall? When it's finished, what is it? When it's not yet finished, what is it? It is posts, wood, planks, corrugated iron, nails, various things. At that stage, we don't call it a hall. Then a skilled carpenter assembles them, hammers them together into a single mass. All those separate things disappear. There are no longer any posts, beams, or rafters – unless you go looking for them individually, you won't see them. They have come together as a single mass, and we call it a hall. It is finished and can be used. Our mind is the same. As long as defilements (kilesa) and craving (taṇhā) are like this – lust, greed, hatred, delusion, ignorance, becoming and birth – it is not yet finished. When they all come together into a single mind...

Ekaṁ cittaṁ – the mind unified as one – then it is accomplished right there.

Ekaṁ dhammaṁ – assembled into one – then it is accomplished in that alone.

title: Ajahn Funn: If the mind still has existence (bhava), that means it is not yet free from suffering. When the mind has no existence, it…
content:
Ehipassiko: Come and See Physical and Mental Phenomena Within Yourself

If the mind still has existence (bhava), that means it is not yet free from suffering. When the mind has no existence, it is finished with existence because it does not grasp anything, does not cling to anything. It is merely the knower. Where would it get existence from? Having heard this, you must reverse the current, turn inward. Ehipassiko – inviting all beings to come and see the Dhamma. See your own physical phenomena (rūpa dhamma) and mental phenomena (nāma dhamma). Physical phenomena are this individual body of ours. Mental phenomena are this mind of ours. Let us come and see. Is this Dhamma wholesome (kusala), unwholesome (akusala), or indeterminate (abyākata)? We must know. Wholesome Dhamma is happiness. Unwholesome Dhamma is suffering. Indeterminate Dhamma – neither happiness nor suffering, neither good nor evil, negating all.

Therefore, when we all want freedom from suffering, we must know that freedom occurs when the mind is peaceful. When our mind is peaceful, then freedom is right there. No need to seek elsewhere. This is the practice.

title: Ajahn Funn: When it’s light, it sees. When it’s heavy, it sees. When it’s dark, it knows that. When it’s bright, it knows that. Don’t…
content:
The Knower Does Not Become Extinct, Does Not Cease

When it’s light, it sees. When it’s heavy, it sees. When it’s dark, it knows that. When it’s bright, it knows that. Don’t go grasping anything. If it’s dark, don’t grasp the darkness. Just take the knowing itself. Take the Knower, knowing that it’s dark. If it’s neutral, observe neutrality. The Knower that is neutral exists. When it’s gone, the Knower that knows it’s gone exists. The Knower exists like that. It does not become extinct, does not cease, does not become nothing. That is why it is called the Knower. Buddho is the Knower. It exists like that. It does not cease, does not become nothing. It has existed from the very beginning. Pubbe te dhammā — phenomena exist like that, but no individual had known them. We must know them for ourselves. The Dhamma exists like that. Before the Buddha’s enlightenment, it existed like that. After enlightenment, it existed like that. But we hadn’t encountered it; we hadn’t yet discovered it. That’s how it is.

Therefore, make the discovery now. Sit in meditation, direct your mind inward, contemplate that knowing itself. Knowing has no self, no being. It is just knowing there, just that one thing — knowing. The Knower is not subject to death, not subject to breaking or destruction, not subject to hunger or poverty, not subject to suffering or hardship, not subject to trouble or annoyance.

title: Ajahn Funn: Within us, everything is complete. The 84,000 Dhamma aggregates, having listened, are not anything far away. When gathered in, they are: the Suttas…
content:
The Mūla-Kammaṭṭhāna: Hair, Body Hair, Nails, Teeth, Skin – Not a Person

Within us, everything is complete. The 84,000 Dhamma aggregates, having listened, are not anything far away. When gathered in, they are: the Suttas – the inhalation of breath; the Vinaya – the exhalation of breath; the Paramattha – the knowing one inside.

The Paramattha is arranged into seven books – the Abhidhamma seven books. When we first hear this, it seems far away, but when explained, it is right within ourselves. Kāmāvacara kusala cittaṃ – the mind that thinks, that constructs, that concocts – where is it? Everything arises from this mind. Wholesome and unwholesome arise from the mind, not from anywhere else. Somanassa – happiness; when our mind delights in wholesome things, it becomes wholesome; when it delights in unwholesome things, it becomes unwholesome. Ñāṇa – knowledge; knowledge is not elsewhere; our mind is the knower. Whatever form we take as an object – beautiful form or ugly form – if we take any form as object, we create a state of being there, establish a state of being there.

When we have heard and listened, ehipassiko – the Dhamma invites us to come and see. He taught to come and see Dhamma, not to go and see Dhamma elsewhere. He taught to come and see our own rūpa-dhamma (material phenomena) and nāma-dhamma (mental phenomena). The material phenomena of our own body – what is there? We assume we are a person, a woman, a man – where is that exactly? We should look closely.

title: Ajahn Funn: Whether good or evil, tassa dāyādā bhavissanti — I will be the heir of that kamma. Whatever kamma we have done, whether merit…
content:
Old Kamma Not Finished, New Kamma Adding – Stop It by Sitting in Samādhi

Whether good or evil, tassa dāyādā bhavissanti — I will be the heir of that kamma. Whatever kamma we have done, whether merit or demerit, we will receive its result accordingly. Kalyāṇaṃ — good kamma. How can we know it? In short: our mind is good, has happiness and ease, light in body and self. That is what good kamma is like, isn't it? Pāpakaṃ — bad kamma. What is it like? The mind is not good — miserable, troubled, agitated, not calm. It goes creating kamma, enmity, danger — heavy, sluggish, drowsy, dull, miserable, hardship — that is bad kamma. Mental kamma (mano-kamma), the mind's inclining. Whatever kamma we incline toward, let go of it. Do not think about it. All kamma — we think it into being. If we do not think it, it does not arise. Old kamma is not yet finished, and we keep adding new kamma. Will it ever end? If you want kamma to end, stop it. Do not create kamma. Even sitting here, you still create it. Bhave bhavā sambhavanti — it creates little and great states of becoming right here. When we see it, cut it off. That is vipassanā. Cut off evil, cut off all mental objects.
